title: Approximating a finite probability space by fair coin flips
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a finite probability space, and let $\delta > 0$. Then there exist a natural number $n$ and a map $\varphi : \mathrm{CoinTape}(n) \to \Omega$ from the length-$n$ binary strings such that, writing $\mu_n$ for the uniform probability measure on $\mathrm{CoinTape}(n)$ (each of the $2^n$ strings equally likely) and $\mu$ for the probability measure on $\Omega$, every subset $S \subseteq \Omega$ satisfies
\[
  \mu_n\bigl(\varphi^{-1}(S)\bigr) \;\le\; \mu(S) + \delta.
\]
hypotheses_covered: Ω is a finite probability space
conclusion holds for every subset S of Ω
replaced:
For any finite probability space $\Omega$ and any $\delta > 0$, there exist $n \in \mathbb{N}$
and a map $\varphi : \mathrm{CoinTape}(n) \to \Omega$ such that for every set $S \subseteq \Omega$,
\[
  \mu_{\mathrm{CoinTape}(n)}(\varphi^{-1}(S)) \;\le\; \mu_\Omega(S) + \delta.
\]
